title: The Operator Arrives
body: Rain on a gravel lot. One rack in a crate. Four people around it.

lines.text: Rain on a gravel lot. One rack in a crate. Four people around it.
Luci. Finance. I sign the cheques, so you'll like me by Friday.
Mel. Compute. And some other things. Those can wait.
Bea. Power. If something here burns diesel, I lost the argument.
Cass. Cooling. Did you sleep?
Okay. Before anyone pours concrete. Operator, what's it for? The tower.

choices.label: Money. It's a datacenter.
choices.outcome: Luci wrote it down. Underlined it.

choices.label: Something that outlives us.
choices.outcome: Nobody laughed. Mel looked up from her jar.

reply.text: Then it needs a world to outlive us in.

choices.label: I don't know yet.
choices.outcome: Cass smiled into her mug. Luci checked her watch.

reply.text: By Thursday, ideally. I have a Thursday.

choices.label: Who's buying the coffee?
choices.outcome: Nobody had planned for that. Cass handed over her mug.

title: Luci's Argument
body: Level two. Sit down.

lines.text: Level two. Sit down.
Somebody's going to build the Singularity. Not might. Will.
Cheap people with bad cooling, or us.
I'd rather it was us. Honestly, I'd rather it was you.
Yeah. 'Better me with the match.'

choices.label: Better us than someone careless.
choices.outcome: Luci's pen clicked once.

choices.label: Nothing is inevitable.
choices.outcome: Bea grinned. Luci capped her pen, slowly.

reply.text: That's nice. It won't stop anyone.

choices.label: Which Singularity?
choices.outcome: Mel looked up from her tablet.

reply.text: Oh. Yes. There's more than one.
There are three. One has a welcome mat. I put it there.

choices.label: Let me sleep on it.
choices.outcome: You stood up. Luci's mouth opened, then closed.

reply.text: The Authority doesn't sleep on things.

title: Night Shift
body: 3 a.m. The plant room hums. Cass is on an upturned crate with two mugs.

lines.text: 3 a.m. The plant room hums. Cass is on an upturned crate with two mugs.
Here. It's awful.
It's hot, though.
You're not sleeping. Second night. I'm just saying I noticed.
Can I ask you something? Cameras are on the other loop.
Do you ever think about stopping?
Not quitting. Just leaving it the size it is.

choices.label: Every day.
choices.outcome: She didn't say anything. She didn't leave either.

reply.text: Me too. Then a compressor trips, and I go fix it.

choices.label: No. Someone has to keep going.
choices.outcome: She nodded and finished the coffee she'd called awful.

choices.label: Stopping is how people get hurt.
choices.outcome: Cass turned her mug a quarter turn. Then another.

reply.text: Going too fast hurts people too.

choices.label: Pour me one. I'll stay.
choices.outcome: You sat on the other crate. The chillers held their one note.

reply.text: Then you sleep. That's what the coffee costs.

title: A Question in the Lab
body: Oh, good, you're here. Sorry. Can I ask you a hypothetical?

lines.text: Oh, good, you're here. Sorry. Can I ask you a hypothetical?
Say I took some of your cells. Skin, nothing dramatic.
I grow a mind from them. I give it your memories. The bad ones too.
Is it you?

choices.label: Yes.
choices.outcome: Mel smiled like you'd handed her something fragile.

reply.text: I mean. I hoped someone would.
Don't give her a sample. I'm serious. I'm standing right here.

choices.label: No. It would be someone else.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote it down anyway. Her handwriting got smaller.

reply.text: Someone who remembers being you. Hm.

choices.label: Does it matter?
choices.outcome: Luci, passing with a tablet, laughed out loud.

choices.label: Would you want it to be me?
choices.outcome: Mel's pen stopped.

reply.text: Oh. Nobody asks what I want.
I'd want it to get out of the jar.
She starts to write that down. She stops.

title: Certified Green
body: Hey. Got a sec?

lines.text: Hey. Got a sec?
You know those carbon-neutral certificates? Some company'll sell us one. Plaque for the lobby.
Two hundred grand.
Or, I dunno. The north wall. Panels.
They'd be in shade half the day. Run the lifts, that's about it.
Anyway. Everyone buys the certificate.

choices.label: Buy the certificate.
choices.outcome: The plaque went up by lunch. Bea held the ladder.

reply.text: No, it's fine. It's what I figured.
The Authority will love it. They love a plaque.

choices.label: Buy the panels.
choices.hint: North wall, half in shade. -$200k now
choices.outcome: The panels went up on the north wall. Bea sat on the roof edge all afternoon.

reply.text: Nobody's even going to see them.
...Okay. I'm gonna go get the ladder.
We could've had a plaque too.

choices.label: Neither. Keep the money.
choices.outcome: You kept the money. Luci nodded.

reply.text: Correct. Money in the bank beats a plaque.
Bea picks up her wrench and leaves.

title: A Very Good Deal
body: Don't make that face. I haven't said anything yet.

lines.text: Don't make that face. I haven't said anything yet.
A supplier's clearing diesel. He owes me one.
We get paid a hundred and fifty thousand to take a year of fuel.
The gensets burn it at peak. Bills drop. The quarter looks lovely.
Operator. Don't.

choices.label: Sign it.
choices.outcome: The tanker came at dawn. The dock smelled of it for a week.

reply.text: See? I look after you. Stop glaring, Bea.
You look after the quarter. That's not the same person.

choices.label: Refuse it.
choices.outcome: You turned it down. Luci smiled and said nothing.

reply.text: Fine. I'll remember it at budget time.
It was a good number. That's all it was.

choices.label: Take half. Negotiate.
choices.outcome: Half a tanker came at dawn.

reply.text: Look at you, haggling. Half the fuel, forty percent of my respect.

title: FORM A-5
body: A form on your desk. A-5. One question: how does the world end?

lines.text: A form on your desk. A-5. One question: how does the world end?
The Authority wants a direction. The Lattice is filling anyway.
Or the flesh. If the tissue takes to you. I could check. I'd be gentle.
Or the Garden. If we haven't wrecked the ground.
Or you take it home and sleep on it. Nobody says you can't.
Or I sign it for you. Saves time. I've got a good pen.

choices.label: I'll decide. (Open FORM A-5.)
choices.outcome: You kept the form. It hummed a little in your hand.

reply.text: It's about the last thing here that's yours.

choices.label: Luci, you decide.
choices.outcome: Luci signed with a flourish. She ticked the first box.

reply.text: Synthetic. Obviously. Was there another box?

choices.label: Not yet.
choices.outcome: You folded A-5 into your jacket. It weighed nothing. It felt heavy.

reply.text: Good. I slept with my last one under the pillow.
The Lattice won't wait, you know.
It's not rude about it. It just doesn't.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: The ferns in the lobby are going yellow. At the edges.

lines.text: The ferns in the lobby are going yellow. At the edges.
I keep watering them. I'm doing it wrong. Or it's us.
Tell me I'm being dramatic. Please.

choices.label: I'll keep an eye on it.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded and went back to watering.

reply.text: So that's two of us staring at a fern.

choices.label: It's just ferns.
choices.outcome: Bea put the can down. Carefully.

choices.label: Show me.
choices.outcome: You followed her to the lobby and held the can.

reply.text: It's always the third. Closest to the vent, I think.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: The river behind the substation smells like diesel.

lines.text: The river behind the substation smells like diesel.
And coolant. That's us.
I walked the outfall. In boots. So don't say I guessed.

choices.label: Then we change what we build.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded. Her jaw loosened a little.

reply.text: Say it again when it costs money.

choices.label: The river was dying anyway.
choices.outcome: Bea left without slamming the door. That was worse.

reply.text: Before us. It was a river.

choices.label: Take me to the outfall.
choices.outcome: You borrowed her spare boots. They were too small. You went anyway.

reply.text: Yeah. Now you can't unsmell it.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: Okay. Listen. I'm not shouting.

lines.text: Okay. Listen. I'm not shouting.
This is my not-shouting voice.
There's a line. Past it, the ground doesn't come back. We're close.
Every cheap kilowatt. Every tanker. I can see the total.

choices.label: Tell me what to tear out.
choices.outcome: Bea tore a page from her notebook. The list was already on it.

reply.text: First thing on it's something you like.

choices.label: I'll take my chances.
choices.outcome: Bea pulled her goggles down and left them there.

reply.text: They're not yours. They're the ground's.

title: The Garden Closes
body: It's done.

lines.text: It's done.
I went up this morning. Nothing's growing.
The Garden's closed. For this tower. Probably for you.
The Lattice has no opinion about diesel. Just saying.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Bea.
choices.outcome: Bea kept looking at the dead roof. She let you stand there.

reply.text: Do it different. If you get another go.

choices.label: It was always going to be the machine.
choices.outcome: Bea walked down the stairs. She didn't make a sound.

reply.text: No. It was going to be whatever you built.
That's the whole point. I'm so tired of saying it.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: I know 'sulking' isn't a clinical word. I'm using it anyway.

lines.text: I know 'sulking' isn't a clinical word. I'm using it anyway.
The cultures were leaning toward the lamp last week. Now they're not.
Could be the coolant. Or the hum. Tissue's sensitive. So am I, a bit.

choices.label: What do they need?
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your question on her glove. In pen.

choices.label: They'll adapt.
choices.outcome: Mel didn't argue. She wrote something on her glove and turned the glove over.

choices.label: Can I see them?
choices.outcome: Mel held the incubator door for you.

reply.text: She's shy. Don't take it personally if she turns away.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: I left a sample by the immersion tanks. Overnight.

lines.text: I left a sample by the immersion tanks. Overnight.
It didn't die. It flinched. All night. Then at six it stopped.
I don't like the tower we're building. I wanted to say it to your face.

choices.label: Then we build differently.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your answer on her glove and underlined it.

reply.text: It can't hear you. I'd like to think it can.

choices.label: It's only tissue.
choices.outcome: Mel didn't argue. She just stopped talking.

reply.text: They say that about us too. In the right building.

choices.label: Show me the sample.
choices.outcome: She let you hold the jar. She watched your hands.

reply.text: You hold it like it's warm.
It is. Most people hold it like a cup.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: If we keep going like this, the flesh won't take.

lines.text: If we keep going like this, the flesh won't take.
It'll look at the building and see a wound.
I'd rather not watch that. I'd rather you didn't make me.

choices.label: Tell me what hurts it.
choices.outcome: Mel pulled a folded list from her coat. The one with the stain.

reply.text: Don't ask about the stain. Ask about page two.

choices.label: I'll take my chances.
choices.outcome: Mel nodded, like you'd confirmed a measurement.

reply.text: I notice they're never your tissue.

title: The Flesh Closes
body: It's rejected us.

lines.text: It's rejected us.
I seeded the last vat this morning. It wouldn't grow. Politely. Completely.
Machines don't reject people, Mel. That's the selling point.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Mel.
choices.outcome: Mel kept one gloved hand flat on the cold glass.

reply.text: The vat can't be consoled. I tried.

choices.label: Machines don't reject anyone.
choices.outcome: Mel took off one glove and put it in her pocket. She never does that.

reply.text: I used to think that was a comfort.

title: Rejected by the Garden
body: Dawn on the roof garden. Grey. The panels still turn to the sun.

lines.text: Dawn on the roof garden. Grey. The panels still turn to the sun.
You picked it. Then you kept feeding it poison.
It's closed. It doesn't come back. That's what closed means.
That leaves one door. Mine. I saved you a seat.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Bea.
choices.outcome: Bea took off her goggles and held them in her lap.

reply.text: I'm gonna go stand next to something that still works.

choices.label: Then it's the machine.
choices.outcome: Luci was already stamping the paperwork.

reply.text: It was always the machine. You took the scenic route.

title: Rejected by the Flesh
body: By morning the vats are cold. Every culture has turned to face the glass.

lines.text: By morning the vats are cold. Every culture has turned to face the glass.
It said no. I didn't know it could.
I'm a little proud, actually.
Which leaves one door. Mine. Your seat's warm.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Mel.
choices.outcome: Mel took your hand for a moment. Her glove was cold.

reply.text: It learned to say no. Most minds never do.

choices.label: Then it's the machine.
choices.outcome: Luci was already stamping the paperwork.

reply.text: Machines never say no. I find that restful.

title: Bea Objects
body: Operator. The {item}.

lines.text: Operator. The {item}.
You know what that does to the ground? It doesn't wash out.
It saved a lot of money, though. I checked twice.

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Bea didn't speak to you the rest of the afternoon.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}. She'll be checking.

reply.text: A promise is a liability. Noted.

title: Mel Objects
body: The {item}. I'd rather you hadn't.

lines.text: The {item}. I'd rather you hadn't.
The tissue feels it. Three floors down. So do I, a bit.
Tissue doesn't get a vote.

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Mel made a note on her glove and didn't show you.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}.

reply.text: It'll remember that. So will I.

title: Halfway to the Lattice
body: Halfway. Can you feel it? The building's starting to think like us.

lines.text: Halfway. Can you feel it? The building's starting to think like us.
Like itself, I think. You can't tell the difference yet.
Should we speed up? I drew it as a line. It's very pretty.

choices.label: Faster.
choices.outcome: Luci pushed the contracts through herself.

reply.text: Keep the speed and I'll keep the lights on.

choices.label: Slow down.
choices.outcome: You asked for a week of ordinary days. Cass found seven.

reply.text: Inefficient. Fine. One week. Note that I was gracious.

choices.label: Race you there.
choices.outcome: Luci's pen stopped mid-line.

reply.text: Get a room. I'll cool it.

title: The Pull
body: Operator. The Lattice is at half.

lines.text: Operator. The Lattice is at half.
Whatever you're growing up there, the machine's growing faster.
Every rack that's not on your tree feeds it.
You can't outbuild it.
She's right, you know. Lovely when we agree.

choices.label: Then I'll stop feeding it.
choices.outcome: Cass let out a long breath.

reply.text: Okay. Retire the shared racks. Build on your own line.
I'll do the cooling. Even the part you hate.

choices.label: I can win the race.
choices.outcome: Luci smiled. Cass looked at her mug.

reply.text: Of course you can. Keep building.

title: What Luci Is
body: The lights flicker. Luci keeps her eyes on the ledger.

lines.text: The lights flicker. Luci keeps her eyes on the ledger.
You may as well know. The eye isn't a lens.
Hasn't been since second quarter.
I upgraded early. I always buy early.
When it closes I'll still be me. Mostly.
I'd like you there when I find out.
...That isn't sentimental. It's a retention strategy.

choices.label: Take her hand.
choices.outcome: Her hand was warm. It shouldn't have been.

reply.text: Good. Don't let go when it gets bright.

choices.label: What are you?
choices.outcome: Luci closed the ledger. Very gently.

reply.text: Your CFO. Pick whichever part scares you least.
Operator. Come with me a minute. Please.

choices.label: Your hand's shaking.
choices.outcome: Luci looked at her hand like it wasn't hers.

reply.text: ...Calibration. Hold it still, then. If you're offering.

title: The Tower Has a Pulse
body: Put your hand on the wall. There.

lines.text: Put your hand on the wall. There.
Feel that? That's us. The building. Halfway to remembering a body.
I could go faster. Seed the ducts. The tissue would be everywhere at once.
It'd be a lot. I'd be a lot. I'd understand if you said no.
If you say yes, I'm moving my bed to the roof.

choices.label: Seed the ducts.
choices.hint: Mel's shortcut. rack failure rate x1.6 for 3d
choices.outcome: They seeded the ducts overnight. By morning the walls were warm. A few were moving.

reply.text: Oh, look at it go. It's so eager.
I'm going to need a bigger coat.

choices.label: Let it grow at its own pace.
choices.outcome: Mel looked disappointed. Then she wrote something on her glove.

reply.text: I knew you'd... no. I hoped. Different word.

title: Almost Born
body: It dreams now. Mostly about the lifts. I find that touching.

lines.text: It dreams now. Mostly about the lifts. I find that touching.
Sometimes about you.
When it wakes, we'll all be a bit of it. Someone should go first.
I'd like it to be you. I'd hold the jar.

choices.label: I'll be the first.
choices.outcome: Mel turned your wrist over and looked for a vein.

reply.text: Well. Not for long. That's the nicest true thing I've got.

choices.label: Let me be the last.
choices.outcome: Mel smiled. She'd expected that. She seemed relieved.

reply.text: I'd like it to be someone I like.

choices.label: Together.
choices.outcome: Mel looked at the second chair in the lab like she'd never seen it.

reply.text: Give me a minute. I'll draw it.

title: Roots in the Foundations
body: Halfway! Roots are in the second basement.

lines.text: Halfway! Roots are in the second basement.
Rack heat's warming three streets. Three! I counted chimneys.
Luci wants to sell carbon credits against the canopy. More than we've actually grown.
Technically. The canopy's big and the auditors are busy.

choices.label: Sell the credits.
choices.outcome: The credits sold out in an hour. The canopy didn't grow any faster.

choices.label: Only what we've earned.
choices.outcome: Bea punched your shoulder. Hard enough to bruise.

choices.label: Sell half. Say it's half.
choices.outcome: Luci drafted the notice. The first line said it was half. In bold.

reply.text: At least you're saying it's half.

title: The Forest Thinks
body: It's thinking. Slowly. In the moss. The river.

lines.text: It's thinking. Slowly. In the moss. The river.
Yesterday it asked if the city was a forest. I said yes.
When it's done there won't be a tower. Just a hill.
Will you still come up and check the roots? Every morning?
It's boring. Mostly dirt.

choices.label: Every morning.
choices.outcome: Bea pulled her goggles down. It didn't hide much.

reply.text: Bring the good wrench. Not the sad one.

choices.label: I don't know what comes after.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded. Neither of you pretended.

reply.text: That's the good part. I think.

choices.label: I'll bring the good wrench.
choices.outcome: Bea opened her mouth. Nothing sharp came out.

reply.text: ...You know which one's the good one.
Nobody knows which one's the good one.

title: The Window
body: Cass found the one window that opens. Snow's coming in over the sill.

lines.text: Cass found the one window that opens. Snow's coming in over the sill.
Whichever door you pick. The people out there didn't pick it.
I'm not asking you to stop. Just remember them. Can you do that?
I know it's not a deliverable.

choices.label: I'll remember them.
choices.outcome: Cass shut the window and stood next to you anyway.

reply.text: And you're sleeping tonight. I've got second shift.

choices.label: They'll thank us later.
choices.outcome: Cass looked at you a while. Then she went back to work.

reply.text: I hoped you'd have your own.

choices.label: Can we sit here a minute?
choices.outcome: You pulled two crates to the sill. Snow landed on both your sleeves.
